name: Drowning in bathtubs, buckets and toilets

0-3m.rationale: CDC data cover all infants under 1 together, so the youngest months are scored conservatively.

3-6m.rationale: CDC: 75% of drowning deaths under age 1 (2018-2019) happened in bathtubs.

6-12m.rationale: Same under-1 bathtub share; babies who sit up are often placed in bath seats, which do not prevent drowning.

12-24m.rationale: Drowning is the leading cause of death at ages 1-4, but CDC's place data for that age mostly point to pools.

24-36m.rationale: Still inside the ages 1-4 group; no bathtub or bucket split is published in the sources opened.

injury_evidence.note: 75% of 73 unintentional drowning deaths among children under 1 occurred in bathtubs (NCHS Data Brief 413).

injury_evidence.cause_category: leaving a young child alone in the bath
injury_evidence.note: AAP reports that an estimated 15% to 30% of caregivers said they left a child under 2 alone in the bath for a minute to just over five minutes.
CDC states drowning causes more deaths among children ages 1-4 than any other cause.

why_it_matters: A young child can drown in only a few inches of water, quickly and silently. Staying within reach and emptying containers after use reduces the risk.

fix_steps.text: Stay within arm's reach of a child in the bath every second. If you must leave, even briefly, take the child with you wrapped in a towel.
Drain the tub right after bath time and empty buckets, pails and other water containers as soon as you finish using them.
Store buckets and containers where a child cannot reach them, and keep toilet lids closed.
Add a toilet lid lock if a toddler can lift the lid.
Do not count on bath seats or rings to keep a child from drowning; they are bathing aids and the adult must still stay within reach.

verify_rule: The tub is drained, toilet lids are closed, and every bucket or container is empty and out of a child's reach.
blind_spots: Adult supervision cannot be seen in a photo
Water left in a container outside the frame
Bathrooms, buckets and tubs at other homes
